facts.spawns: Bella Seed Bella Bud Immaculate Red Flower Breathtaking White Flower Gorgeous Yellow Flower
taunt: “You dare terrorize my beautiful home!? Begone, insects!” Belladonna alternates between rapidly circling in place or remaining stationary in the room’s center. During the former, she will fire 4-way streams of spearlike shots along with 4-way shotguns of leaves. During the latter, she will either fire slower rings of leaves and Slowing pink petals, or fire rings of blue berries.

“You will be as food to my children!” Bella throws out 12 Bella Seeds that form a ring around her. The seeds will then sprout and begin circling her, firing slowing pink petals towards her while firing spreads of Sickening spears outside of the ring. These petals alternate between firing directly towards the boss, or firing at an angle so they form a tight ring around the boss before vanishing.

“Be consumed by my young!” Belladonna becomes invulnerable while the sprouted Bella Seeds become vulnerable. The Seeds fire in the same pattern that they did before, but Belladonna will now maintain “beams” of spear shots in an X-pattern, constraining the player’s movement. She will also throw her bombs more frequently and in greater amounts.

“Roots, flowers, vines, destroy these villains!” Belladonna becomes vulnerable and summons a large amount of Red, White, and Yellow Flowers around the map that fire radial shots which have varying effects. Flowers can be destroyed, but will all self-terminate and respawn after some time has passed

“You are nothing more than nutriment for my roots!” Bella begins moving around the map. She alternates between firing rapid pairs of leaves alongside spreads of spears, or Armoring herself and firing dense rings of blue berries. Note that flowers will continue to spawn during this phase.

“My thorns will drive you away like the locusts you are!” Flowers stop spawning and Belladonna spawns 4 invincible Bella Buds that orbit her at various distances, firing multi-directional spear shots. Belladonna herself will be throwing single berry bombs at the player.

“I will not be silenced, I will not be destroyed!” The four Bella Buds position themselves in the corners of the room before each fire a 4-way spiral of armor piercing Stunning spear shots that rotates clockwise. The arms of the spirals will sweep across the entire map in a periodic pattern. They will also be firing petals everywhere except in front of themselves. At the same time, Belladonna will be pulsing short-ranged waves of Confusing leaf bullets and releasing a large number of parametric Slowing berry shots.

“My children…aid me…” Belladonna becomes invincible and releases periodic undodgeable waves of Quieting petals. Her and her minions maintain the behavior from the previous phase, but the Bella Buds are now vulnerable. All four must be killed to push Belladonna out of the phase.

“YOU WILL NOT LEAVE HERE ALIVE!” Belladonna begins aggressively lunging at players. Every time she lunges, she will either fire a radial barrage of wavy leaves, a radial barrage of wavy spears, or a storm of pink petals that form either a star-shaped or diamond-shaped formation. Between attacks, she will go briefly invincible and fire a single large spear at the player.

taunt: “Knights, to arms!” Beisa spawns in four Oryx Elite Brutes , which initially fire directed spreads of white shots that inflict Bleeding. If they are buffed, the shots will be orange and also inflict Sick.

“To your positions!” The Brutes follow behind Beisa closely. Beisa himself will deploy a banner in the center of the arena before circling it with his troops, firing 2-way bursts of white and grey slashes. After reaching 95% HP, he will move to phase 1B.
“Move in!” Beisa chases players while firing the same pattern. His troops will follow closely and fire shots. After reaching 90% HP, he moves to phase 2.

“My forces are infinite!” The Oryx Elite Brutes start patrolling back and forth along the horizontal axis of the arena. They switch to rapidly firing single aimed white (orange when buffed) arrows and occasional shotguns of armor piercing knives.

“Spineless runts! Stand your ground and fight!” The Elite Brutes begin moving in a square pattern around the center of the arena and fire both white shots and armor piercing knives. Beisa will chase players, firing spreads of spinning axes to his sides while launching dense shotguns of slash projectiles in front of him. He will also periodically release a ring of larger, boomerang axe projectiles.

“Falconers, strike from above!” At 70% HP, Beisa summons 4 Oryx Elite Falconers that initially attack with bursts of blue bolts (larger spears if they are buffed). The Falconers will also be launching Oryx Elite Falcons in many phases, invincible foes that slowly fly after players while shooting slow, short-ranged spreads of black spikes. After flying for long enough, Falcons will flash red and explode into lingering rings of shots. Falcons are marked on the minimap like other enemies.
“Everyone together!” Beisa will repeat Phase 1A, except now with the support of his Falconers. At 65% HP he moves to phase 3B.
“Surround the enemy!” Beisa repeats Phase 2A with the added minion support and transitions to phase 4 after reaching 60% HP.

“Disrupt the opponent’s movement!” Beisa changes his troop formation. The Oryx Elite Brutes will start patrolling back and forth along the horizontal axis of the room, and the Oryx Elite Falconers will do the same along the vertical axis. The Brutes will fire spreads of arrowheads, and the Falconers will fire pairs of blue bolts and single silver arrowheads, although they will not summon Falcons for this attack.

“Dodge, parry, come on!” Beisa commands the Elite Brutes to follow him once more, while the Elite Falconers start moving around the edges of the arena, firing inwards at players and launching Falcons. The Brutes switch to attacking with multi-directional knives.

“Keep them covered!” The Elite Falconers start following Beisa, while the Elite Brutes will begin independently chasing players as a unit. The Elite Brutes will start firing shotguns of armor piercing knives, while the Elite Falconers will stop firing and exclusively (and rapidly) summon Falcons.
“Assassins, formations!” At 40% HP, Beisa summons four Oryx Elite Assassins that will initially attack with multi-directional bursts of Slowing green shurikens (bigger if buffed).
“Keep steady!” Beisa repeats Phase 2A/3A again, but with all of his minions. At 35% HP, he transitions to 5B.
“CHARGE!” Beisa repeats Phase 2B/3B with all of his forces, transitioning to his final phase upon reaching 30% HP.

“Control the outside!” The Elite Falconers and Assassins start patrolling/circling (respectively) the center of the map. The Falconers fire spreads of silver arrowheads and the Brutes will fire spreads of bleeding shots while following Beisa. Beisa will choose a corner of the arena and move to it before moving around the edge of the arena in a counter-clockwise direction, firing directed spreads of devastating spears and pairs of wavy fire shots.

“Flank them!” The Elite Assassins start following Beisa, the Brutes start circling the middle area, and the Falconers start patrolling a zig-zagging path across the arena’s horizontal axis (but will not summon Falcons). The Brutes will be firing 2-way spreads of knives. Beisa will chase players with his cohorts, rapidly firing rings of black spinners and throwing V-shaped bursts of exploding blade projectiles, their AoEs telegraphed by red crosshairs.

“Strike through, contain all ends!” The Elite Falconers start following Beisa as the Brutes/Assassins patrol the horizontal/vertical axes of the arena. The Brutes fire two-way “walls” of knives, the Assassins fire pairs of purple bolts (bigger if buffed), and the Falconers fire pairs of blue bolts (bigger if buffed). Beisa and his squad will patrol the room’s diagonal axes, while he fires rings of white shurikens and multi-directional purple slashes. He will pick a random corner to start and then follows a deterministic pattern of corners to continue to, ultimately exploring three of the four corners of the arena fully (the attack will end before he can patrol the last corner).
facts.upon_entry: “Overachieving weaklings. You are far out of your depth.” First room cleared: “Your kind perceives power in yourself for getting through the cannon fodder Oryx calls his castle minions.” Second room cleared: “My subordinates are trained better than that. They know what it means to learn and improve, exalting themselves.” Third room cleared: “Grumbling in my domain does not suit me. Come forward, face your challenge head on!”

taunt: “You think you can defeat me? Then let me show you the true power of Xil!” Daichi summons the four Elementals to circle their respective corners of the room and fire rings of status shots. He himself will be in the middle of the room, firing a four-armed spiral of purple spinners that periodically changes direction, along with periodic rings of Pet Stasis shots.

“Fear the Elements!” Daichi teleports to a corner of the room and summons an Elemental, which will become the new target and attack players while Daichi supports it with his own shots. The Elemental he first chooses will be random.
“ENOUGH! You fought well but now it’s time for you to die.” “Unlimited power!”

facts.attack_phase: “Try my latest concoction!” “Have a deadly potion!” “For Science!” “My automatic turret will destroy you!” “Side effects may include your death!” “Don’t worry, your death will be documented closely.” “If my calculations are correct, this will hurt you.” Dr Terrible will wander around, occasionally throwing Green Potions , Turret Attacks , or both. They are all dangerous and deal high damage, especially the Green Potions , which can kill an unmaxed character with low defense instantly. There are four Red Gas Spawners (which are pretty lethal all the same) in the room that may also shoot waves of slow moving bullets during this phase. Each of these four Red Gas Spawners will not always fire. During this phase Dr. Terrible can be damaged.
facts.base_hp: 33,750 ( Boss Adaptive HP Scaling ) DEF: 25 EXP: 6,000 Location: Mad Lab
facts.retreat_phase: “Time to feed my pets!” “You’ll make a nice snack for my creations.” “Time to delegate your death to my minions.” Dr Terrible will retreat to the bubble in the center of the room. While he is in the bubble he is invulnerable and he summons Escaped Experiments , Mini Bots , and Rampage Cyborgs from the cages on the east and west sides of the room. The Red Gas Spawners will turn off during this phase.

facts.phase_1_taunt: ”Hah! I’ll drink my rum out of your skull!” ”Hah! I’ll cut ye into parrot crackers!” Dreadstump attacks the nearest player with rapid yellow shots while keeping his distance.
facts.phase_2_taunt: ”Arrrr…” Dreadstump starts circling players, alternating between single cutlass shots and single cannonballs. Occasionally he will flash red and say ”Eat cannonballs!” before Armoring himself and firing three larger cannonballs with higher velocity and damage.
facts.phase_3_taunts: ”I’ll turn you into a hearth-rug!” ”Ye trifle with the strongest fleet on the high seas!” Dreadstump runs to the other side of the ship and taunts ”Fire the cannons!” The four cannons near the front of the ship and the two near the back will start firing large cannonballs down the ship’s length. Meanwhile, Dreadstump will circle the ship’s mast, alternating between a pair of cutlass shots and a triple-shot of cannonballs.

facts.darkness_attack: Rotate with the “spiral” of small dark bullets. Accelerate further when a black laser comes to avoid being hit by the next one. If you are doing this correctly, your rotation with the spiral will automatically avoid the rainbow blasts.
facts.fire_attack: There is a wide area where the fire bullets don’t converge. Find it. The orange laser shots amd rainbow blasts aren’t too much of a threat if you are moving at a slow pace. Make sure not to cross the wall of orange lasers because you will tank multiple 100-damage bullets.
facts.hp: 16,000 DEF: 20 EXP: 2,500 Realm Score: 500 Minimap Icon: Location: Sprite Forest
facts.ice_attack: Similar to the Artifical Sprite God , find a moving gap within the spiral and move with it. Unless you are a melee class, stay far away so the Elder Sprite Tree doesn’t shoot its ice bolts, same with the rainbow blasts.
facts.magic_attack: Make sure to get in between the gaps between the bolts, as well as rotating to avoid the endless onslaught of magic swirls. In the case it fires the almost unavoidable ring of rainbow blasts, either try to move back or get behind an object.
facts.nature_attack: You can go in between the laser shots here, and make sure to watch for the two spirals, as their projectiles move extremely fast.

facts.activation: ”Welcome. Come closer to accept your reward.” “Come in… come in.” “Ah, fresh meat. I must thank you for the souls…”
facts.base_hp: 45,000 ( Boss Adaptive HP Scaling ) DEF: 20 EXP: 30,000 Minimap Icon: Location: Ice Cave
facts.repeats: ”Fools! You though it SO EASY!!” “You will not have him. He is mine.” “HAHAHAHA”
taunts: ”The ice I throw is of my construction, but when it hits you it means destruction!” “Ice is cold, blood is thick, you being alive makes me sick!” “Bad puns I may use to cause offense, but the pain you will feel shall be immense!” “Icicles, rend their flesh!” “I will cut you to shreds!” “Your soul will soon nourish me.” “Your entrails will make fine decorations!”
”Please, do not let him consume my soul…” “End it… quickly! Before he returns.” “You must destroy me. It is the only way to banish him.” “I can barely hold on. Please. Do it.”
”Noooo! Shades, come to me. Protect the corpus.” “YOU’LL NOT HAVE ME! ESBEN IS MY VESSEL!”

The color of the banner will resemble the stat it will grant.

facts.carp_emperor: Rarely, the Carp Emperor Encounter will spawn and become visible as a red dot on the map. To make its first phase vulnerable, it is necessary to hold the fishing bobber over its tail in the center of the pond. Upon its defeat, the pond will return to its normal fishing state.
facts.creatures_of_the_deep: Enemies from the Deep Sea Abyss spawn instead of colored orbs, and will begin attacking. These need to be defeated in order to continue fishing.
facts.fishing_frenzy: Far more ripples appear than normal, letting players catch far more fish than normally. Glover requests an infinite amount of fish. Destroying enough orbs before the end of the event counts as a success.
facts.fishmen: Fishmen from the Ocean Trench spawn instead of colored orbs, and will begin attacking. Unlike normal Fishmen, these feature some armor piercing attacks that make them more dangerous. These need to be defeated in order to continue fishing.
facts.piranhas: A shoal of Piranhas spawn instead of colored orbs, and will begin attacking with low damage sick projectiles. These need to be defeated in order to continue fishing.
facts.school_of_fish: Most ripples are the same size, exclusively spawning a certain tier of fish. Glover will only request that rarity of fish.
facts.there_are_five_rarities_of_fish: common, uncommon, rare, epic, and mythic. Fish of these rarities can be used to get rid of light blue, green, dark blue, orange, and purple orbs respectively. Once all orbs are gone, Glover will spawn a fishing treasure chest that can be destroyed for rewards. There are three tiers of chests he can spawn, with harder fishing tasks granting better chests. If enough time passes without the fishing task getting completed, all remaining orbs will despawn, and no reward will be given.

facts.orb_shotgun_phase: Septavius first flashes and throws out 5 random ghost minions around him. He will then start firing fast White Orbs in a shotgun of three aimed at the nearest player. In this phase it is recommended to clear the minions while circling the boss.
facts.quiet_and_confuse_phase: Septavius fires out 4 Confuse stars aimed at each corner of the room while constantly firing oryx spirits that inflict Quiet. Septavius slowly wanders toward the closest player during this phase. Be wary during this phase because the boss will change to the next phase without warning.

taunt: “Let it snow!” Jack Frost throws bursts of eight bombs around himself, throwing four in an X and four in a plus. All eight bombs will land at the same time, but are split in two “parts”, with the first four bombs being thrown earlier, but having a longer throwtime.

“Your dreams of a White Oryxmas shall only be nightmares!” Jack Frost fires pairs of wavy Slowing blue stars and teal ice bursts at the nearest player, while firing two four-shot spreads of snowballs that slowly rotate counterclockwise.
“All I want for Oryxmas is your grave!” Jack Frost alternates between erratically moving and chasing players, firing rapidly alternating 3-way shotguns of Weakening snowflakes.
“Prepare to be jingle bell ROCKED!” Jack Frost chases players with single icicles, before briefly stopping in place and releasing 8-way streams of ice arrows.

“Heroes, did you know…that you are about to perish!” Jack Frost fires two oscillating streams of Paralyzing blue icicles, periodically lunging at players. The first stream is always aimed north, while any later streams will pick a random cardinal direction.
“My two front teeth are about to sink into your skull!” Jack Frost runs away from players while firing shotguns of small snowballs, and occasional 2-way bursts and rings of larger, slower snowballs.

“It’s the most wonderful time of year for you to die!” Jack Frost circles the nearest player, then stops in place and fires a massive 4-way shot-machinegun of snowballs, alternating between in a cross shape or a plus shape after each movement.

“Your death will come upon a midnight clear!” Jack Frost releases an oscillating petal-like pattern of blue stars akin to a Djinn , paired with a predictive shotgun of either 3 or 4 Unstable aqua bullets.

“THIS WILL BE YOUR LAST ORYXMAS!” Jack Frost becomes stationary and starts firing a 4-armed spiral of blue orbs that inflict Unstable, alongside blue crescents fired around himthat Slow. He will periodically interrupt the spiral with rapid 4-way shotguns of blue orbs.

taunt: “It’s down to the drink with ye either way! Har har harrr!” Jon Bilgewater alternates between two attack patterns (starting with a random one), switching between them every few seconds. When switching attacks, he will briefly pause and flash red while invulnerable.

“Arrrrrghhh, ye won’t long in the crossing firepower of two men-of-war!” The exit to the room seals off as the cannons lining the sides of the room activate, constantly firing barrages of cannonballs from both sides of the room. Jon will remain still in the center of the room and alternate between two different attack patterns using the same logic as his previous phase:

“Ahoy, Bartholomew! Treat this bilge rat like your mates in the gibbet cages!” Jon goes invulnerable and opens the parrot cage in the arena, releasing his pet parrot Bartholomew along with 3 Deadwater Macaws. The Macaws orbit Jon while firing single blue feathers, while Bartholomew chases down players with shotguns of green and red feathers. The parrot cage will periodically release additional Deadwater Parrots that follow Bartholomew while firing shots.

“Scurvy dog! Look what ye did to my ship! Yer blasted pieces will be shark bait!” The floor of Jon’s ship starts breaking apart, revealing hazardous tiles of Dead Water that deal damage and slow players on contact. He switches to his next attack patterns:

“Ye won’t get away with this! Deadwater will hound ye across the seas for the rest of yer days, savvy?” The floor of the ship breaks down even more, revealing more Dead Water. Jon switches to his last attack set.

“Shiver me timbers! No landlubber will best the Pirate King!” “Dreadstump was a DreadCHUMP! Yer no match for a real Pirate King!” At any point within his final phase, Jon may randomly decide to use this attack instead of a regular one. It is generally used less commonly than his usual attacks.

taunt: “I’ll run you down!” The Flying Machine chases after the target while firing pairs of red waves and rings of slow mines that clutter the arena during the chase.

“You think you can keep up with me?” The Flying Machine charges in a straight line at the target, shooting flames perpendicular to its movement and leaving behind a trail of flames that deal continuous damage and inflict Armor Broken and Exposed . Every time it touches a wall, it will readjust its aim to the nearest target before charging again.

“Missile Barrage!” The Flying Machine becomes Armored and chases players while firing rings of turning gold waves and rapidly spawning Seeking Bots that chase players. If a Bot gets close to a player, it will flash white before exploding into a ring of shots.

“Spray and Pray!” The Flying Machine moves to one end of the room and fires an oscillating barrage of slow red orbs in front of itself, while also firing spreads of waves behind itself to catch anyone hiding behind it. It will repeat this several times at different ends of the room.
“Evasive Maneuvers!” The Flying Machine circles around the room, firing spreads of red waves and rings of red arrowheads.

facts.phase_1: -The two waves of Pet Stasis projectiles aren’t aimed at any player, they simply rotate around the Brute. If you stay between them and rotate with them, not only will you not get hit by them but you’ll also most likely dodge the big mossy shots and the rush attack.
facts.phase_2: Paralyze or Slow the Warriors so you don’t have to deal with their random movement pattern. The sooner they die, the better.
facts.phase_3: The Brute will be Armored when it’s vulnerable, so keep those Cwands and Dbows ready for it.

facts.taunt: “You can’t harm me while my warriors are protecting me!” The Brute spawns several Warriors far away from it and becomes inactive. He is invulnerable until the Warriors are killed.

facts.darkness_form: Only their Silencing Shot includes Aim Tracking, so circling while attack it is a solution. Additionally, you can moving from left to right, right to left while it is shooting you.
facts.fire_form: The only projectiles that you have to worry about are the wavy ones that it fires in a clockwise-motion, which deal damage. Otherwise, you can stand still, as the silencing chains that they shoot deal 0 damage.
facts.hp: 3,500 DEF: 12 EXP: 250 Location: Sprite World
facts.ice_form: The weakest of about all enemies in the Sprite World, if you have more than 10 defense, you can just stand still while firing away. Be careful not to stand too close to him while he changes form, as you might tank a full shotgun of projectiles.
facts.magic_form: Probably the trickiest to dodge of all, they will shoot wavy projectiles in a wide shotgun, so stand a safe distance away and back off when both of the middle bolts intersect.
facts.nature_form: Deadliest of all, it shoots 4 incredibly wide projectiles that do heavy damage after traveling backwards a bit. Circling this enemy is a viable solution, but don’t stand too close behind it, as it’s projectiles travel a bit backwards before firing forward.

taunt: “A breach? This can’t be right. You must leave this place at once!” During the first phase, Null will shoot out bursts of omnidirectional boomerang shots which cause unstable. After a while, Null will teleport to one of the four cardinal corners of the room and shoot two rotating spreads of Paralyzing bullets that return to it, before teleporting back to the center of the room and repeating the pattern. After enough damage is taken, Null will become invisible and spawn the first minion group.

“Enable the firewalls!” Null will reappear in the center of the room and become vulnerable to attack again. The edges of the room will be replaced by Exposed Code for the phase, which deals rapid damage if stood in. Meanwhile, Null circles the center of the room clockwise and doesn’t shoot any projectiles outside of Armor-Piercing Unstable bombs, but Firewalls will move horizontally along the top and bottom of the square, shooting armor piercing firewaves towards the center of the room.

“Prepare to feel the DISCONNECT between our realities!” Null reappears in the center of the room and chases players with shotguns or radial blasts of sequential “shockwaves” that Slow. One quadrant of the room will flash white twice and turn into black terrain that doesn’t block projectiles or enemy movement, but disconnects players who don’t move off it in time (like bridges in The Shatters ). Once a quadrant has gone back to normal, another will begin flashing and the process will repeat until Null takes enough damage to trigger the next phase.

“I hope you’re ready to crash and burn!” This phase is a combination of phases 3 and 5. Null will rotate around the center of the room clockwise shooting slow moving confusion balls, while the edges of the map will be filled with Exposed Code patrolled by bullet shooting Firewalls. Like in phase 5, Null will make a quadrant of the map flash white twice before disconnecting any players still standing in it. When enough damage is dealt, the final minion groups will spawn.
“The system is crashing!” Null reappears at the center of the room and shoots 6 rotating streams of slow moving blind stars. The streams start by rotating clockwise, but can switch directions.

facts.phase_1: Circle around the boss while shooting it. You can also just dodge between the shots in the spirals while shooting the boss. The spirals aren’t dense enough to force you to rotate. Ranged classes can easily go between the two cleavers as long as there isn’t a purple vortex between them.
facts.phase_2: Sidestep the chains, avoid walking into the deccelerating shots once they slow down. Paralyzing the boss can be helpful. Melee classes should be careful not to get by the chains when they boomerang back.
facts.phase_3: Stand in the large gaps between the spirals and rotate around the Harvester. Sidestep any chains that come your way. Avoid running into chains that get shot in the way you’re moving.
facts.taunts: “Come to donate your organs?” ”A fresh batch of organs has arrived!” ”Fresh meat ripe for the taking!” The Organ Harvester stands in place while firing 5 spirals of armor-breaking purple vortexes that rotate clockwise. There are fairly large gaps between shots in a spiral. He also fires twin cleavers at a nearby player.

pages.summary: For Oryx the Mad God 1, see this page. For Oryx the Mad God 3, see this page. Once Oryx is defeated here, players can use the Oryx Runes at the three monuments spawned after his death in order to access Oryx’s Sanctuary for a chance to battle Oryx’s strongest incarnation.
pages.title: Oryx the Mad God 2

presentation.summary: For Oryx the Mad God 1, see this page. For Oryx the Mad God 3, see this page. Once Oryx is defeated here, players can use the Oryx Runes at the three monuments spawned after his death in order to access Oryx’s Sanctuary for a chance to battle Oryx’s strongest incarnation.

facts.archer_tips: Oryx will be on the move throughout the second half of the fight, which may cause more chaos than needed. To combat this, make sure you aim your ability at Oryx so that he becomes paralyzed, or at the very least slowed. This can help knights use their ability to stun him! Try to keep Oryx permanently paralyzed if possible in a fashion similar to how knights may keep him permanently stunned.
facts.assassin_tips: Assassins are considered the best class to use in a Wine Cellar, as their poisons are ideal for Oryx 2, who is vulnerable for quite some time, and doesn’t move around too fast until the second “chasing” phase. Use off-center screen to lob poisons and get tons of easy damage in.
facts.base_hp: 65,000 (+20% [13000 HP] per player in Dungeon) DEF: 60 EXP: 20000 Location: Wine Cellar
facts.circling_tips: Circle Oryx 2 clockwise if Oryx is directly in front of or behind your character . Circle Oryx 2 counter-clockwise if Oryx is to the left or right of your character . getting confused while circling in the wrong direction will send you charging into Oryx’s Shotgun. Remember that your “left” key will make you go “down” when confused, so press “left” to retreat (assuming Oryx is in front of you).
facts.knight_tips: Try to dodge the status effect stars and run in and stun. Running in a straight line towards O2 won’t be a very good idea. Try to circle Inward to close the distance and stun. Make sure to have a lot of MP wine or MP potions so you can keep stunning! Make sure to run out BEFORE the stun wears out. But be careful, a missed stun can mean death! WARNING: When Oryx changes phases, he may become unstunned with a very high chance of instantly killing any nearby character, even 8/8 knights.
facts.priest_tips: It is best to have a tiered wand in the first stages, as the tiered wands pierce through his minions and are able to reach Oryx with no problem. For the second stage however, it is best to use a Crystal Wand or Conducting wand; as they generally have higher damage.
facts.rogue_tips: Leave before you turn visible! If you are a rogue you should run next to Oryx, stay for about 3 seconds (assuming you have a cloak that is Twilight or up) then go back so that you don’t get shotgunned by Oryx. Getting slowed could mean that you are unable to get out of the range of Oryx’s shotgun when you uncloak.
facts.wizard_tips: Sometimes Oryx will get pinned to a wall. You can go to the other side of the wall and shoot your spell. This is recommended when the wine cellar contains few people, and when most of the minions in the hallways of the cellar have been cleared out.

facts.base_hp: 562,500 ( Boss Adaptive HP Scaling ) DEF: 75 EXP: 200,000 Minimap Icon: Location: Oryx’s Sanctuary
facts.note: One Greater Potion of Life and one Greater Potion of Mana are guaranteed drops for all players that achieved soulbound damage, although there is a non-guaranteed chance for one additional greater potion of each to drop.
facts.summons: Bomb Artifact (number varies, invincible) Portal of Oryx (x4, invincible) Inner Dance Artifact (x4, invincible) Outer Dance Artifact (x12, invincible)
taunt: “Your armor will crumple before me!” (if Exalted) ”Foul insects! Your armor will crumple before me!” Oryx crouches slightly and chases the nearest player, firing powerful 3-shot bursts of slash projectiles. He will also be throwing 3-round volleys of bombs on either side of him about every second.

“There is nowhere to run!” (if Exalted) ”Belligerent creatures! There is nowhere to run!” Oryx levels his sword and chases players while firing rapid shotgun blasts of large white bullets. He will also periodically release a dense ring of smaller white arrowheads, and occasionally lunge at the nearest player.

“Accept your fate!” (if Exalted) ”Defiant scoundrels! Accept your fate!” Oryx raises his sword and chases players while firing a barrage of spears around himself. He will also be sporadically firing Quieting white orbs around himself while using a directed spread of large arrowheads.

“Fleeing is futile!” (if Exalted) ”Lowly pigs! Fleeing is futile!” Oryx wraps himself in a purple tornado (gold in Exalted phase) and circles rapidly while chasing players with 8-directional lines of severely damaging crescent projectiles that pierce armor.

“My shield is enough to smash you to pieces!” (if Exalted) ”Miserable mutts! My shield is enough to smash you to pieces!” Oryx’s shield glows blue (gold in his Exalted phase) as he charges in a straight line at the nearest player, firing Stunning bullets in a cone in front of him. He will also fire large bullets perpendicular to his movement while leaving a trail of stationary spinners behind him. Note that he will frequently and sharply change the direction of his charge to try and ram the nearest player.

“You cannot escape from my control!” (if Exalted) ”Meaningless whelps! You cannot escape from my control!” Oryx braces himself, slightly raises his shield , and releases a large number of lingering fireball projectiles that inflict Weak. He then chases players with pairs of slashes and shotguns of arrowheads.

“Melt before my fury!” (if Exalted) ”Mindless brutes! Melt before my fury!” Oryx wreaths himself in flames and lunges at players while detonating Dazing AoE blasts on himself. Every time he finishes a lunge, he will stop to release two dense rings of white arrowheads.

“Stand back in cowardice, but you will find no safety!” (if Exalted) ”Disgusting creatures! Stand back in cowardice, but you will find no safety!” Oryx wraps himself in a black tornado (silver in Exalted phase) and circles in place while firing dense, overlapping spirals of small and large white arrowheads that rotate in different directions.

“There is nowhere to hide!” (if Exalted): ”Worthless scullions! There is nowhere to hide!” Oryx spins and circles counterclockwise around the middle of the room (right outside the center carpet), firing rapid overlapping spirals of small and large white arrowheads. This is effectively the same as his Barrage phase, but with added movement.

“I will strike you down!” (if Exalted) ”Abominable knaves! I will strike you down!” Oryx twirls and circles counterclockwise around the edge of the map, firing rings of Exposing white spinners while firing shotguns of large arrowheads towards the center of the room.

“Every slash shall slice through your pathetic defenses!” (if Exalted) ”Wretched slime! Every slash shall slice through your pathetic defenses!” Oryx raises his sword, remains still and repeatedly detonates red AoE blasts on himself while swinging his sword, sending large waves of slash projectiles towards players as well as in the opposite direction. These waves have some gaps in them that players can weave through.

“Gaze at my power, for it shall be your last sight!” (if Exalted) ”Rebellious wretches! Gaze at my power, for it shall be your last sight!” Oryx holds his sword in a two-handed position and remains still while rapidly firing gradually widening shotguns of extremely powerful arrowheads at the nearest player. He will also be sporadically firing Quieting white orbs around him.

“Panic and scream, moments before you are blasted into oblivion!” (if Exalted) ”Incompetent fools! Panic and scream, moments before you are blasted into oblivion!” Oryx pulls out a Bomb Artifact and chases the nearest player, while rapidly spawning invincible Bomb Artifacts in groups of 4. These will repeatedly detonate AoE blasts on themselves while moving away from him in a cross pattern (alternating between along the cardinal or intermediate directions). Bomb Artifacts self-terminate after travelling a certain distance.

“The ground quakes from my splendor!” (if Exalted) ”Deplorable slugs! The ground quakes from my splendor!” Oryx repeatedly stabs his sword into the ground and throws out a massive amount of Sick bombs around him, four times. He will always throw red, blue, yellow, and green bombs, but they are functionally identical. Each burst of bombs has a “safe spot” depending on its color (see the Tips section for more details).

“The cosmos shall rain down my wrath upon you!” (if Exalted) ”Loathsome worms! The cosmos shall rain down my wrath upon you!” Oryx points his sword at the sky , remains still, repeatedly detonates red AoE blasts on himself, and calls down meteors from the sky, telegraphed by red circles marking their landing spots. Upon landing, meteors will explode into a ring of 6 fire bullets.

“My dominance extends throughout the universe!” Oryx summons 4 invincible Portals of Oryx to assist his attacks. They have 3 different orbit distances depending on what attack Oryx is currently using, and attack with single shots, streams, pairs, or spreads of normal or wavy fire bullets that inflict Pet Stasis, depending on Oryx’s current attack. The Portals fire outwards if they’re close to the center, inwards if they’re close to the edges, and both ways if they’re midway. The Portals will temporarily vanish between attacks and whenever Oryx is successfully staggered.

“Dance, you helpless creatures! DANCE!” Oryx summons special Bomb Artifacts around the room’s perimeter, which quickly form an inner and outer ring - 12 black ones on the outer ring, and 4 white ones on the inner ring. The Artifacts then start rotating clockwise while detonating red AoEs on themselves, dealing heavy damage to anyone caught by them.

“Before crushing the life out of you, I will show you why my power is utterly beyond question!” At 55% HP, Oryx will go invulnerable and move to the center of the room before transforming, the tiles in the arena also turning bright to signify this change. His armor becomes silver and gold, and his sword ignites with flame as the Mad God ascends to a new level of power - Oryx the Exalted God . ”Behold, the glory of a god above all others! I am absolute! I am…EXALTED!”

“The heavens are mine to command!” Oryx’s Holy Beams are now upgraded. Every three Holy Beam strikes (and immediately upon hitting this HP threshold), he will horizontally sweep the map with sequential rows of Holy Beams - either one row that sweeps in one direction (either from left-to-right or right-to-left), or two rows that sweep the room in opposite directions (starting from the middle and sweeping outwards, or starting from the edges and sweeping inwards). These beam walls will do significant damage to players caught in them due to the overlapping AoEs, but can be crossed with good timing. Note that beam walls travelling in only one direction will travel slightly faster than those travelling in two directions.

“Despicable mortals! A single realm freed is meaningless! Millions more remain in my grasp!” Oryx teleports to the center of the room as all Portals and Messengers despawn. Holy Beams strike the edges of each of his arena’s 4 quadrants in order, destroying them and sending them plummeting into a dark void (the beams will do damage, but the vanishing ground can be safely stood on) - eventually reducing the arena to only the cross of carpeted ground. The four carpets will be destroyed by Holy Rays, leaving only the central platform that Oryx stands on - and even the central platform will soon be destroyed (although it can still be stood on), leaving the whole arena as an empty, starry void with planets revolving within.
facts.taunts: First hitting HP threshold: ”Kneel to your ruler! My strength is without equal!” Using attack: ”FALL BEFORE MY CELESTIAL STRENGTH!”

presentation.summary: For Oryx the Mad God 1, see this page. For Oryx the Mad God 2, see this page. Oryx 3 can be considered the “final boss” and the most difficult enemy in Realm of the Mad God.

facts.assassin_tips: Assassins are considered the best class to use this fight, as their poisons are ideal for Oryx 2, who is vulnerable for quite some time, and doesn’t move around too fast until the second “chasing” phase. Use off-center screen to lob poisons and get tons of easy damage in.
facts.circling_tips: Circle Oryx 2 clockwise if Oryx is directly in front of or behind your character . Circle Oryx 2 counter-clockwise if Oryx is to the left or right of your character . getting confused while circling in the wrong direction will send you charging into Oryx’s Shotgun. Remember that your “left” key will make you go “down” when confused, so press “left” to retreat (assuming Oryx is in front of you).
facts.hp: 48,750 (+20% [13,000 HP] per player in Dungeon) DEF: 60 EXP: 20,000 Location: Battle for the Nexus
facts.knight_tips: Try to dodge the status effect stars and run in and stun. Running in a straight line towards O2 won’t be a very good idea. Try to circle Inward to close the distance and stun. Make sure to have a lot of MP wine or MP potions so you can keep stunning! Make sure to run out BEFORE the stun wears out. But be careful, a missed stun can mean death! WARNING: When Oryx changes phases, he may become unstunned with a very high chance of instantly killing any nearby character, even 8/8 knights.
facts.priest_tips: It is best to have a tiered wand in the first stages, as the tiered wands pierce through his minions and are able to reach Oryx with no problem. For the second stage however, it is best to use a Crystal Wand or Conducting wand; as they generally have higher damage.
facts.rogue_tips: Leave before you turn visible! If you are a rogue you should run next to Oryx, stay for about 3 seconds (assuming you have a cloak that is Twilight or up) then go back so that you don’t get shotgunned by Oryx! Getting slowed could mean that you are unable to get out of the range of Oryx’s shotgun when you decloak.
facts.wizard_tips: Sometimes Oryx will get pinned to a wall. You can go to the other side of the wall and shoot your spell. This is recommended when the fight contains few people, and when most of the minions have been cleared out.

facts.earth_smash: -Counter- intuitively enough, the best way to avoid eating those is to stay as close to the Statue as possible. The Statue won’t use them on players that are less than a screen away from it, but if you get back and sit one or two screens away to regen or to type in the chat you WILL die. Note the Earth Smashs are each airbourne for about 3 seconds so the further away you are, the faster each Earth Smash will fly at you which may take a half second to notice.
facts.grappling_hook: -The Hook counts as an enemy and can be Slowed with the right timing. This method is however very unreliable due to how precise you have to be, so you’re still better off circling the Statue to dodge it.

taunt: “Rise, my vessel! Aid my assault and we may breach the realm itself!” The Spirit orbits the Possessed Oryx Statue, firing large X projectiles in a V shape in front of him. He will sometimes switch to firing flurries of small X projectiles that follow a curving path.

“Brute force will not save your pathetic lives now!” After a bit, he will turn invulnerable and move to the Statue’s death location. Then he will turn vulnerable again and fire 4-directional bursts of multicolored waves that Armor Break and inflict various other debuffs. The waves are fired in a spiralling pattern so that they cannot be dodged by standing still.
facts.taunts: “Agh! I am weakened!” “Stay away! You must not tamper with the spiritual plane!” “My host has collapsed, but my spirit remains!” After the Statue is killed, the Spirit of Oryx will rapidly chase players while firing shotguns of large white bursts. He will also fire lines of skull-like projectiles to the side of him. Once he hits certain HP thresholds, he will switch to Phase 3.

Being able to ascend to higher dimensions, she took residence in the Third Dimension where she commands an army of cubes against the realm. Outside of the fourth dimension, the Tesseract Goddess’ form is quite unstable.

taunt: “One more step forward and you get wet!” The Gardener cycles between rings of decelerating Slowing bubbles, Armor Breaking water bolts, and accelerating armor-piercing splashes in order. He will also frequently throw out a ring of six green water balloons around him that deal heavy AoE damage, cycling through 4 throw distances in order of increasing radius.

“It is very important to water the garden!” The Gardener throws out a ring of Water Buckets that rotate around the perimeter of the arena, pulsing damaging blue AoEs and periodically firing water splashes towards the center of the arena. Note that there are two gaps in the ring of Water Buckets, opposite from each other (and thus two gaps in the converging bullet rings).

“Let me show you my watering cans!” All Buckets of Water despawn as the Gardener throws out two golden Gardener Lawnmowers that orbit him in opposite directions at two different orbit distances, leaving behind trails of stationary water bullets. The Gardener will be firing a 2-way clockwise spiral of twin water bucket shots that pierce armor.

facts.accelerating_spreads: The Lich King fires large spreads of accelerating blue shots in several directions. Purple Crescents: The Lich King fires many silencing purple crescents in all directions
facts.bone_shots: The Lich King chases players while firing twin exposing bone shots at them, with the occasional 6 shot spread. Purple Shots: The Lich King wanders in place while alternating between firing slowing purple triple shots in the cardinal or diagonal directions.
facts.bone_tower_chase: The Lich King chases players while firing Bone Towers in front of and behind himself, which constantly detonate an exposing white AoE on themselves. He also shoots large spreads of accelerating blue shots to the left and right of himself. Bone Tower Indicators: The Lich King goes to the middle of the setpiece and becomes stationary, firing lines of silencing purple crescents above and below himself and in an X pattern, while also shooting large spreads of quieting purple shots either in random directions or at players who get close. During this phase indicators will constantly appear around the setpiece, with Bone Towers rising out of the ground in those areas, detonating a painful AoE before disappearing.

taunt: “Quit messing with my operation!” The Skeyper aggressively chases and circles players for a few moments. After circling for a bit, he will briefly flash before dashing at players with two diverging streams of Crystal Bolts that Silence. He then repeats the process, circling again.

“Get your own portals, freeloaders!” The Skeyper becomes stationary and creates a large patch of darkened ground around him. He will then start firing an omnidirectional barrage of boomeranging key bullets that pierce armor. There are two rotating gaps in his barrage for players to dodge in (on opposite sides of the circle), but every second he will be firing spreads of Paralyzing yellow spinners at the player closest to himself, often targeting said openings.

“Ack, get away from me!” The Skeyper lets out a massive but harmless Slowing AoE, before quickly fleeing from nearby players. He will be erratically firing Slowing white spinners behind him as he flees, while constantly throwing Slowing AoE bombs.

taunt: “Running away? Cowards!” The Wanderer spawns four portals that form a grid of green bullets. She then chases players while firing aimed swords, converging bursts of blue blades, and spreads of purple blades behind her. She also summons a Wanderer Shadow which periodically teleports to fixed points on the map at random, firing a ring of oscillating purple shots before vanishing.

“Dodge this!” After marking their locations with harmless green shots, the Wanderer creates four blue swords that rotate around her, along with a ring of purple circles at the edge of the arena which rotate in the opposite direction. She will also remain still in the center of the arena and fire a storm of small blades in all directions.

“Ram through!” The Wanderer alternates between Armoring herself in the middle of the arena while firing swords in all directions, and chasing players with rings of blades and aimed walls of small swords, gaining brief invulnerability when changing patterns. Periodically, Wanderer Shadows will spawn from the corners of the arena, charging in a straight line while firing arrowheads of swords.

“Sword flurry!” The Wanderer stays in the middle of the room and fires a 3-armed spiral of axes and rings of blades, while periodically shooting three streams of swords that form a spinning ring to trap players with her. Four portals will also rotate around the arena, firing slow spreads of green arrowheads inwards and rapid spreads of green shots outwards.

“Shadestep!” The Wanderer circles the middle of the arena while firing aimed spreads of swords. Four portals in the corners of the arena fire spreads of green spinners, while four more portals at the cardinal points fire sweeping streams of swords. All of the portals will fire towards the center of the arena.

facts.summons: Treasure Artifact
taunt: “Let’s see how well you can negotiate for your lives!” Gemsbok rapidly teleports between his designated points as well as the center of the room, firing 4-round bursts of “chains” of purple shots that inflict devastating damage and multiple status effects (each chain consists of a Treasurer Wave, Bolt, Spinner, Trishot, and Shuriken in order, which respectivelySlow/Expose/Unstable/Armor Pierce/Petrify). He will also be throwing out pairs of gems - these explode in AoE blasts that inflict different status effects depending on what color they are (Green for Sicken, Red for Armor Break, Blue for Silenced, and Yellow for Daze). Every time he teleports to a new location, he will fire a ring of armor-piercing Pet Stasis bolts in his wake.

“Heads I win, tails you lose!” At 40% HP, Gemsbok turns invulnerable and teleports to the center of the room (he will also heal himself to 40% HP to prevent overdamaging). He will then spawn 3 special passive Treasure Artifacts around him, one of which will be flashing . Gemsbok then quickly shuffles the coins around for a few seconds, before letting them turn vulnerable. If the coin that was flashing at the start is damaged enough , it will rebound and stagger Gemsbok for a significant amount of time, stunning, immobilizing, and armor breaking him. While he’ll recover prematurely upon hitting an upper limit for damage dealt to him in this state (~15% of his max HP), if enough damage is dealt to him in the stagger, the majority of this phase can be skipped. “Wha-” “NO!” (after stagger ends) “YOU’LL PAY FOR THAT CHEAP SHOT!”

“Impoverished rats! Laugh all you want, but the rich will always take their place above you!” At 10% HP, Gemsbok armors himself, teleports into the center of the room and begins firing 2-way shotguns of purple shot chains at players (with three chains in each shotgun), starting with chains aimed at the northeast and southwest quadrants of the room. The direction in which he fires the shotguns will slowly rotate clockwise. He will also be throwing large amounts of jewel bombs in cross-shaped bursts, each burst 45° offset compared to the preceding one. The bursts always have a fixed order of bombs (red innermost, then blue, then green, then yellow) and explode in sequence from innermost to outermost. Every few seconds, he will throw out a Treasure Artifact, which charges players while firing Cursing purple spinners to the sides. However, the Treasure Artifacts orbiting the room’s center will vanish, although the outer ones will still persist. Gemsbok will turn invulnerable at the start of this phase and remain invulnerable until he has fired three shotguns.
facts.taunts: “Your lives are now forfeit!” “The realm’s gold stands beneath your feet!” “Let’s make some CHANGE in the realm!” At 70% HP, Gemsbok teleports into the middle of the room, instantly summons 3 Treasure Artifacts if they are not already active, and becomes invulnerable, twirling his scepter and pointing it forward as it pulses with golden energy. He will also heal himself to 70% HP to prevent overdamaging and start firing massive, 2-way shotguns of his purple shot “chains” that slowly rotate clockwise, with four chains in each shotgun; he will also be rapidly throwing jewel bombs aimed at players to discourage standing still. These chains are initially aimed at the bottom right and top left quadrants of the room. He cannot be harmed while performing this attack, and players must simply survive.
facts.upon_entry: “I always knew some unclean wretches would wander from that filthy cellar someday…” First room cleared: “Ah, so these are the serfs Oryx prattles on about.” Second room cleared: “Through the tax offices, are they? How I loathe their dirty presence near my vault…” Third room cleared: “How utterly indignified of them to harass my cabinet like this! Their place will be made clear soon enough, I suppose.”

At its true range, this bow outdamages the Warmonger at around 20 defense and always outdamages the Bow of the Void.

facts.effect_s: Within 4.5 tiles Inspired for 6.5 seconds. Tempo Change: Control the rhythm of the drums to match the situation Ability 1: Crescendo Effect on self: Berserk for 5 seconds. Blitz Rhythm: Greatly increases shot speed, whilst boosting effective weapon range Ability 2: Adagio Party Effect: Healing [40/s] (+1 per WIS over 75) for 4 seconds within 5.5 sqrs Tranquil Rhythm: Lowers your shot speed, but boosts effective weapon range
facts.note: Both modes will increase your shot range by 25% when using a regular bow. However, since this lute does not modify acceleration speed, certain weapons have odd interactions. Deaccelerating weapons like the B.O.W. will end up with more range when using Crescendo, while accelerating weapons like the Garland Bow will have more range with Adagio.

Enemies here often drop potions of Defense, Speed, and Attack, along with a wide variety of portals to Dungeons that give access to all non-life/mana stat potions. The area can be identified by its light-brown dirt ground surrounding a grass-filled circular center marked with ruined buildings.

facts.be_prepared_for_what_may_come: You should avoid lava at all costs, as it slows your movement, deals damage, and renders you vulnerable to the attacks of approaching enemies. Demons of the Abyss are DANGEROUS: Be more cautious with them than the ones found in the Realm. Lava only hurts your feet: Simply rotate your camera angle so that your feet stay on the lava bridges to avoid being hurt by it.
tip: If you have an adequate amount of defense on your character, you will be able to stand close to the Idol and be able to consistently damage it, albeit having to endure the shots sent at you by the Idol. You will be amazed by how weak the Idol is without the help of its lava!

When you are fighting brutes, you can run around in circles and shoot behind yourself to allow yourself to damage them while avoiding their own shots. Brutes are agile, but not as agile as you - use that to your advantage!

facts.the_golden_oryx_effigy_has_two_phases: one where he is completely vulnerable, and another in which he is Invulnerable . In his first phase, he has four Treasure Oryx Defenders that orbit him. These idols can do 80 damage if you are wearing absolutely no armor, so steer clear. After you kill the four defenders, the Golden Oryx Effigy will go into his second phase. He will then start to fire Medusa-style bombs everywhere as he starts his rage phase - once he calms down he spawns his little satellite minions again and you just rinse and repeat. Just remember that you cannot hurt him until all of the satellite guards are dead. Decent DPS can make this fight go by quickly, but if you find yourself struggling, retreat to the edges of the room to heal. Paladins and Priests are good classes for simply surviving the fight if you are inexperienced, but more powerful players can focus on damaging the boss as fast as possible.

facts.the_cultist_hideout_has_a_rather_simple_: just brown corridors with enemies found in small clumps within the hallways. Although not as labyrinthian as the Lost Halls, the Hideout does occasionally feature forks in its paths. Whenever a hallway diverges into two others, head to the hallway that does not have a beam over it at the entrance. The hallway leading to the bosses will never have a beam at its entrance when it comes from a split. The hallways with beams over them simply lead to dead-ends. After beating through the halls, you will find a large room with a pentagram in the center. In that room, the second boss battle of the Lost Halls awaits you.

facts.the_dungeon_is_a_timed_gauntlet: players are tasked with killing waves of enemies as fast as they can, with the Alien Satellite in the center giving warnings to how much time is left. Every time the stage is cleared of enemies, more will spawn in to replace them. There are three waves with 4 sub-waves each - for a total of 12 waves - and every fourth wave has a designated boss that can drop loot.

pages.summary: Like the rest of its kind, it is a timed gauntlet dungeon where players race against the clock to dispatch waves of enemies for loot. This dungeon is a source of various stat increase potions, the set tiered Alien Core: Corrosion and the untiered Foramite Staff, Acidic Slasher and Corrosion Cutter. It is also the source for the Forax Technology.

facts.the_dungeon_consists_of_three_stages: the Gates, the Graves, and the Mausoleum. Each stage is a square arena, with each getting slightly bigger. There is no way to return to previous stages.

facts.how_to_kill_step_one: Clear the room of the smaller demons before shooting the Idol. If you do accidentally shoot it, be ready for a difficult fight.
hp: 30,000 (+20% [6,000 HP] per player in Dungeon) DEF: 40 EXP: 2000 Location: Heroic Abyss of Demons Counts toward God Kills Immune to Paralyze Immune to Stun Immune to Stasis Levitates off ground Quest Boss
24,000 (+20% [4,800 HP] per player in Dungeon) DEF: 50 EXP: 68 Location: Heroic Abyss of Demons Immune to Stasis
facts.step_3: Various spots of the room should be getting filled with lava and going back to normal. Just move to safe spots without getting caught in the lava. Keep attacking when you get the chance until it dies and the lava disappears. Get the Vit and hopefully a whitebag.
facts.step_two: Once the room is clear, begin using your weapon on the idol. If you are using a Wizard, Knight or any ability that deals massive damage, use it. For knights, use an Ogmur and a Colossus Shield on it quickly.
tip: Sometimes, if you stand very close to the idol and find the right spot (it will be one of the cardinal directions), you can stand next to the idol and only get hit by its small shotgun. It will not throw lava at you, and can be killed laughably easily.

When you are fighting only brutes you can run in circles and shoot behind you, because the brutes shoot forward and they follow the player, walking straight into your shots, while you easily dodge theirs.
The Heroic Abyss is a great place to build up base fame. So if you are looking for a godlands dungeon to farm for fame, the Heroic Abyss is the way to go.

facts.the_dungeon_is_a_timed_gauntlet: players are tasked with killing waves of enemies as fast as they can, with the Alien Satellite in the center giving warnings to how much time is left. Every time the stage is cleared of enemies, more will spawn in to replace them. There are three waves with 4 sub-waves each - for a total of 12 waves - and every fourth wave has a designated boss that can drop loot.

pages.summary: The dungeon is the source of various stat increase potions, the set tiered Alien Core: Warp, and the untiered Warlord Wand, Gaseous Glaive and Blazon Bow. It is also the source for the Katalund Technology. Wormholes to Katalund spawn randomly when the Alien UFO is slain.

Every time the stage is cleared of enemies, more will spawn in to replace them. There are three waves with 4 sub-waves each - for a total of 12 waves - and every fourth wave has a designated boss that can drop loot.

It is also the source for the Malogia Technology.

facts.there_are_two_main_types_of_phases_in_th: DPS phases and Danmaku/Lantern phases. DPS phases act similarly to most conventional boss fights in that you must damage the boss as much as possible. The more you damage the boss, the faster the phase goes. All bosses are always Armor Broken whenever they are vulnerable, so armor-piercing items and even rare ability items such as the Shield of Ogmur are ineffective against damaging them.

difficulty: Medium Typical close-range units that will try to run at you and clobber you with short-ranged shots. They can easily be beaten by backpedaling, but don’t try to tank them: they can hurt.

Low Ranged attackers that will pepper you with rapid spreads of arrows, much like a real Archer or Huntress would. While it does look intimidating, the arrows do little damage: the only time you should watch out for them is if you are not maxed in defense or are Armor Broken.

Low These guys have much longer range than the majority of the enemies and will try to snipe you with single, high-speed bullets. Their shots are hard to dodge but don’t hit hard, so don’t mind too much if you’re hit by several.
Low The in-between of the Hosts that attack with rapid mid-ranged shots. Still not really a threat due to the below-average damage of their shots.

Low A long-distance attacker with extremely fast shots. They churn out a ton of bullets in a short time, but like their bow-wielding brethren do low damage per shot. If you have maxed defense, don’t worry. If you’re Armor Broken, stay away from them.
Low A mid-ranged attacker with moderately powerful piercing slashes. They move quickly and dodge your shots by circling you. Blocking this using a wall is the fastest way to put them to rest.

Medium-Very High Extremely fast enemies that will run at you and explode in your face. Their shots slow and inflict substantial damage: enough that they can instantly kill lightly armored characters should they explode on them. Since they have deceptively high health, don’t bother trying to kill them: just try to avoid their blast. Be very careful when clearing the path between rooms as these pests can move through the obstacles, leaving you with very little time to react. Tanking all their shots can mean instant death for an unmaxed character.

Low More of a hazard than anything, these things are scattered everwhere. When killed, they will explode into a ring of Quieting waves. Since their blast is rather spread out, it is easily avoided, but never stand directly on one: their waves deal rather high damage per hit.

Medium These enemies are liberally scattered throughout the dungeon and are summoned by the Blob Colony. They have different health values (from least to most HP: Scout, Normal, Guardian) but all do the same damage and have the same attack: a shotgun of Sickening bullets. They are not a threat individually, but will swarm you without hesitation, at which point their damage begins to stack up due to your disabled healing. Don’t let them pile too much damage on you and you should be fine.

Medium-High These guys are significantly more threatening than the previous couple of foes. They pack decent health and use highly damaging pairs of shots while chasing you down. From medium range, they can’t even hit you and you can just fire away. But at point-blank range, their shots hurt a lot. Simply backpedal and don’t let them get too close, and you should be able to kill it.

Very High These nasty enemies attack with nonstop shotguns of blue bullets that shred right through players. Each bullet deals extremely high damage - 140 base each - so eating the shotgun will spell a swift death for even melees. Because it’s piercing, don’t even try hiding behind teammates. Fortunately, its shotgun is far less dangerous at long range, so feel free to engage it from there.

High A deadly enemy that aggressively chases down players while rapidly firing single shots that deal extremely high damage. Despite only having one shot, its firepower is immense and must not be underestimated. In addition, it constantly detonates deadly explosions around itself to make sure nobody can get close to it. Melees, stay out of this: each explosion hits for 110 base damage, and it detonates about 2 per second. Since it only has 1 shot, zigzagging backwards is highly effective in deterring them.

Very High The appropriately-named Horror Maw is arguably the deadliest normal enemy in the dungeon. Packing the highest HP of a normal enemy (4000), this beast utilizes one of the oddest shot patterns the game has to offer: namely, firing a 4-round burst of red bolts that curve outwards before converging on a single point. Needless to say, this attack is rather hard to dodge and incurs massive damage, especially if you are unlucky enough to be at the intersection of the shots. Fortunately, it has a blind spot in front of it. Unfortunately, it has an extremely dangerous shotgun that it fires to ward people away from said blind spot. Their shot is so complex, however, that the Horror Maw itself seems to struggle with it: simply standing still will result in you being too close to get hit by the curving shots, and too far away to trigger the shotgun. For those unwilling to commit to this stressful strategy, the easiest way to deal with them is still from far away, while retreating.

Medium-High These enemies will attack with aimed Red Bombs that deal relatively high damage. That’s not the main threat, however: that would be the swarms of Parasitic Blobs and Blob Guardians they spawn in periodically. Since they are thrown out in such large numbers, it is easy to get bombarded by their Sickening shots and chunked for a huge amount of health. Don’t assume that they will just circle idly around it: the Blobs will occasionally give chase to the nearest player. Nonetheless, piercing weapons are great for clearing out the Blobs, and the Explosive Barrels are especially effective against the Blob Colony since it will heavily damage its swarm of minions as well. Melees are not recommended to attack this, as the swarm of Blobs will rapidly shred players that get close enough.

Medium-High These things do not have any actual attacks. Instead, they rely on a small squad of invincible Pterasites to defend itself. The Pterasites carry bombs, and will fly at players attempting to drop the bombs on them. Once dropped, the bombs will have a priming time of about half a second before exploding into a ring of Slowing shots, and the Pterasite will return to the Colony to retrieve another bomb. The Pterasites are not too dangerous, but the explosions from their bombs will inflict serious damage if stood on. Stay wary: the Colony itself can manually lob Pterasite Bombs at players. Also make sure to go straight for the Colony: the Pterasites and their bombs are invulnerable.

Medium-High This is likely the deadliest of the Colonies due to the fact that it can physically attack you. When it sees a player, it will begin firing parametric bullets in all directions, forming a swarm of Quieting, highly damaging shots around it. It will then begin targeting the nearest player with directed shotguns. These colonies are extremely difficult to take down with melees, so ranged characters should step in and snipe it from afar: the actual range its swarm can hit from is rather low. Simply sidestepping will be sufficient enough to avoid its directed attacks.

facts.note: enemies will be split by their weapon type for organization. These puppets all use bows to attack from a distance. Beware the Archer and Huntress Puppets , as they both inflict Slowed : the former with its arrows and the latter with its AoE grenade. The Bard Puppet is a more defensive enemy, buffing itself with Inspired and Armored , making it more tanky due to the latter. These puppets all use swords to deal close-up damage. The Knight Puppet inflicts Stunned , which can be annoying when trying to clear out enemies. The Warrior Puppet behaves similarly to a Warrior wielding a Helm of the Juggernaut , as during its “Berserk Phase” it will stand still, become Armored, and rapidly fire shots towards the nearest player. Although the shots themselves are relatively harmless if you have high DEF, they still pose a threat nonetheless due to being fired out rapidly. Finally, the Paladin Puppet is the most annoying enemy out of the group, as it will occasionally enter a “healing phase” in which it rapidly heals a whopping 170 HP every second. Do as much damage as possible before its healing phase, or bring someone to help clear it if you’re in a group. These enemies use wands to deal damage from a long distance. The Priest Puppet constantly attempts to stay 3 tiles away from the nearest player, while also periodically healing itself for 100 HP. It’s less annoying than the Paladin Puppet as it doesn’t heal as frequently nor as much, while also having less defensive stats. The Sorcerer Puppet throws yellow grenades which spawn Puppet Bombs that explode into circles of shots. A second pair of Puppet Bombs will spawn from the explosion of its previous Puppet Bomb, meaning if multiple Puppet Bombs are spawned, you’ll be walking in a literal minefield. Finally, the Summoner Puppet is unique in that it can spawn other puppets to its aid. If you want to fully clear a room of enemies, it is recommended to nip it in the bud and destroy the Summoner Puppet first. These enemies use staves to attack from afar, albeit with slightly less range than the previously mentioned wand-wielding puppets. The Mystic Puppet is the only enemy in the dungeon to fire Pet Stasis inflicting shots. While having no effect on players without any pets equipped, it can be detrimental to new players who are very dependent on their pet’s abilities, such as healing. The Wizard Puppet fires an omnidirectional burst of shots on itself, which are very slow. The only real danger from this enemy is sitting on it; otherwise it is very easy to dodge its shots. The final staff puppet is the Necromancer Puppet , which fires Bleeding shots. The shots do a fair amount of damage combined with the damage/time debuff of Bleeding, so try to keep clear of this enemy. These puppets all wield daggers along with being quite fast. The Rogue Puppet is another annoying enemy that occasionally turns Invisible, making it harder to attack. Do remember that its red dot on the mini-map still appears, so you can try to attack there. You could also fire where the Rogue Puppet is firing from and hope you eventually destroy it. Next is the Assassin Puppet , which throws AoE grenades that deal a fair amount of damage. They can even be thrown if the enemy itself isn’t loaded in, resulting in grenades being thrown over walls. This lone enemy is the reason why AFKing in this dungeon can result in death. The Trickster Puppet will create a copy of itself upon detecing a player, and then attempt to circle the player along with a copy. The copy has identical stats, except its shot doesn’t deal any damage. You can use this to your advantage and attack the Trickster Puppet that does deal damage to you. These enemies all wield katanas and attack from mid-range. The Ninja Puppet only fires a single shuriken shot, which, while dealing a high amount of damage, is also extremely easy to dodge, since it’s aimed solely at the nearest player. The Samurai Puppet spawns a wall of shots inflicting Exposed near its target. Try not to move around too much near this enemy as to avoid accidentally walking into its walls of shots. The Kensei Puppet moves similarly to the Priest Puppet, staying a few tiles away from the nearest player but still maintaining some distance. It will fire a long-range brown sheath projectile along with a short-range purple slash, both of which can be easily sidestepped. It also constantly detonates a damaging AoE attack on itself.

facts.a_word_of_caution: Use of an Electric pet or other abilities to inflict Paralyzed Limon will cause her to fire a radial blast of shots similar to the Staff of Extreme Prejudice. In the first phase (and during her Darkness and Ice Form), the high possibility of Limon being near or on top of your character makes Paralyze strategies extremely risky, as her radial burst of shots has a high chance of instantly killing low-defense characters in close quarters. Save paralyzing abilities to deal damage during Limon’s Darkness Form in her second phase, and avoid getting within a dangerous range of her if using an Electric pet. If you want to reduce her mobility safely without risking an insta-killed character, use Paralyzing abilities from afar or opt for using abilities inflicting Slowed instead.
facts.darkness_form: This form may also be more difficult to dodge, as it can be hard to predict Limon’s movement pattern. Try to stay away from the corners of the stage, as those are where the many rainbow stars are being shot out. As for Limon herself, attempt to circle in her direction, that way, you’re never too close to Limon and can continue to deal damage while simultaneously sidestepping her shots. This can be hard if you accidentally circle into her direction instead and get sat on.
facts.ice_form: You have two options of attacking Limon here. Either stay in the middle and dodge both the arena shots and Limon’s shots, or stay close to the bottom of the arena and deal damage there. It is preferrable to stay below Limon as she won’t aim her shots at you, but rather above her. This can make dodging all the attacks less stressful. From then on, simply sidestep into the gaps of slowing shots from the arena.

facts.magic_form: For this form, you must chase Limon as she travels from corner to corner throughout the arena. Make sure to pay attention to the huge spiral of shots diving the arena occasionally, as a mistimed maneuver can easily cause a swift death.
facts.native_sprite_god: Sprite Star Pet Skin Potion of Attack
facts.nature_form: This form of Limon may be more difficult, as there are much more shots to dodge. Attempt to rotate with Limon in order to deal damage, while also trying to micrododge the green beams as you move around. You could also sit in the middle and damage her from afar if you’re a ranged class, although you’ll now have to micrododge Limon’s own attacks.

facts.the_sulfurous_wetlands_has_two_ut_weapon: the Brambletooth Tachi and the Bogwood Crook . The Brambletooth Tachi has more range than tiered tachis, making it more difficult to land shots with, but it does beat out the T12 tachi. However, it becomes ineffective on high DEF enemies, making it less viable in endgame content. Meanwhile, the Bogwood Crook is a staff that functions similarly to highered tiered bows, having a main damaging shot along with two side armor-piercing shots. The Crook has two spots with true range, meaning you have to attack from specific distances if you want to land all three shots at once. If you can consistently land the shots though, then it beats out the T13 staff.

facts.honey: Honey will not hurt you, however it acts like the quick sand in the Ancient Ruins or a Tomb of the Ancients - the longer you stay in this substance, the more it slows you down. If you stay long enough, you will get stuck there, moving at extremely low speeds, which might be very deadly if enemies are around you. Avoid staying in honey for a long time, and don’t step in there during the boss fight!
facts.note: These tips are general tips for all classes, and all players. Also, if you have lots of defense, some tips may not apply.

facts.the_boss_can_drop_2_honey_themed_ut_s: the Honey Scepter and the Orb of Sweet Demise . The Honey Scepter’s only redeeming quality is that it hits more targets than any other Scepter. However, it’s lackluster damage for general use makes it very weak, though it’s still good for quick crowd clearing early-game. Meawhile, the Orb of Sweet Demise actually has more utility even through mid-game, as it’s one of the few orbs to inflict Slowed and Stasis simultaneously. Due to its short but spammable ability along with its common drop rate from an early-game dungeon, it can legitimately be used as a swapout mobility-impairing orb midgame, at least until a better one is found.

taunt: “You’ll be short work for my fragments! Your weapons mean nothing against me as long as they’re sustaining my barrier.” The Tesseract Goddess throws out its four fragments, staying Invulnerable as the fragments attack. The fragments move in a set pattern diagonally clockwise around the middle area of the room. They will also shoot simple two way slowing shots aimed at the player. Meanwhile, the Tesseract Goddess herself will rapidly detonate AOE bursts on itself, while also throwing the occasional pink Silenced bomb at the nearest player. With every fragment defeated, they will return to the boss, Square Ether will begin covering the room, limiting your movement, and the Tesseract Goddess will slowly gain new attacks:

“My fragments could not have been disabled so easily!” Once all four fragments have been defeated, the boss will continue her same attacks, but remove her pink Silenced bomb. She will continue this until she is pushed to the next phase.

“Steel yourselves! My cubytes will reduce you to nothing for your transgressions against the Mad God.” With her fragments defeated, the Tesseract Goddess will spawn four Cubytes , this time with new attacks. The cube fragments will slowly rotate clockwise and begin slowly shooting two way tentacles of shots both inwards and outwards of the room. The fragments then speed up and shoot out rapidly. The boss meanwhile will occasionally shoot out a pink bomb that inflicts Silenced towards the nearest player. Your goal now is to rotate with the Cubytes and damage them in order to get to the next phase. As a Cubyte loses HP, it slowly shoots slower until only shooting everyone couple of seconds. This can allow you to quickly move to another Cubyte and damage them sequentially. Once all the Cubytes are defeated, they will shrink and slowly disappear.

“Imperfections such as you so-called heroes must be eradicated.” “You misshapen miscreants will perish in the lower dimensions, having lost all form!” Once pushed enough, the Tesseract Goddess will despawn her clone, and will teleport back to the middle of the room. She will reappear instead colored red and purple, similarly to the Dirk of Cronus , and begin repeating her phases prior, this time much harder. She will repeat her first phase, spawning her fragments, but they will instead circle counterclockwise and will shoot much faster. Instead of Square Ether, Cronus Ether will flood the corners of the room, and will not disappear until the very end of the battle. Finally, the boss herself will gain attacks twice as fast, gaining all of them at two fragments instead of all four. Use the same strategies as for Phase 1. Rotate with the fragments and watch out for the telegraphs to preempt the attacks.
“My fragments have failed me yet again!” Destroying all the fragments once again removes the Tesseract Goddess’ invulnerability.

“But my cubytes have returned stronger than ever!” The Tesseract Goddess will respawn her Cubytes, which are also colored after the Dirk of Cronus. Similarly to the Cubytes from Phase 2, they will slowly shot and slowly rotate, although this time counterclockwise, before speeding up and shooting tentacles rapidly. Meanwhile, the boss will throw a pink bomb to the nearest player, instead inflicting not silence, but Quiet . Employ the same strategy as before. Rotate with the Cubytes and kill them off, and move to the next Cubyte by crossing tentacles quickly.
“Look sharp! Your fate in the drifting void draws near!” The Tesseract Goddess moves to the middle of the room and grows in size, before rapidly choosing between three random attacks:

“Inconceivable! My perfection is unparalleled!” Once the boss finally takes enough damage, she will shrink down in place before dying and dropping her loot, with the Cronus Ether also disappearing from the arena.

facts.the_dungeon_is_a_timed_gauntlet: players are tasked with killing waves of enemies as fast as they can, with the Alien Satellite in the center giving warnings to how much time is left.
